title: CentOS LXC VM is not reachable after reboot with snapd
description:
### Please confirm

- [x] I have searched existing issues to check if an issue already exists for the bug I encountered.

### Distribution

CentOS

### Distribution version

9-Stream

### Output of `snap list --all lxd core20 core22 core24 snapd`

```shell
> snap list --all lxd core20 core22 core24 snapd
Name    Version         Rev    Tracking       Publisher   Notes
core20  20260105        2717   latest/stable  canonical✓  base,disabled
core20  20260211        2769   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
core22  20260128        2339   latest/stable  canonical✓  base,disabled
core22  20260225        2411   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
core24  20260211        1499   latest/stable  canonical✓  base,disabled
core24  20260317        1587   latest/stable  canonical✓  base
lxd     5.21.4-1374f39  38368  5.21/stable    canonical✓  disabled
lxd     5.21.4-aee7e08  38767  5.21/stable    canonical✓  -
snapd   2.73            25935  latest/stable  canonical✓  snapd,disabled
snapd   2.74.1          26382  latest/stable  canonical✓  snapd
```

### Description
```shell
Hi,

Moved bugreport to LXD from Snapd https://bugs.launchpad.net/snapd/+bug/2136699

---

To trace PostgreSQL snap issue on CentOS: https://github.com/canonical/postgresql-snap/issues/26
I have tried to deploy the latest Snapd but LXC VM gone after reboot.

STR:

> lxc launch --vm images:centos/9-Stream -c limits.cpu=6 -c limits.memory=16GiB -d root,size=100GiB centos-lxc
> lxc shell centos-lxc # this works well, you can reboot VM many times, all OK

Install Snapd to CentOS LXC VM using https://snapcraft.io/install/postgresql/centos

> sudo yum install epel-release
> sudo yum install snapd
> sudo systemctl enable --now snapd.socket
> sudo ln -s /var/lib/snapd/snap /snap

This work. Snapd looks OK. Try to reboot VM and reconnect it quickly
(it will be successful once, so you can catch logs and see Relabeling there):

> [root@centos-lxc ~]# journalctl -f
...
> Dec 17 09:56:48 localhost selinux-autorelabel[531]: Warning: Skipping the following R/O filesystems:
> Dec 17 09:56:48 localhost selinux-autorelabel[531]: /run/credentials/systemd-sysctl.service
> Dec 17 09:56:48 localhost selinux-autorelabel[531]: /run/credentials/systemd-tmpfiles-setup-dev.service
> Dec 17 09:56:48 localhost selinux-autorelabel[531]: /run/credentials/systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service
> Dec 17 09:56:48 localhost selinux-autorelabel[531]: Relabeling / /dev /dev/hugepages /dev/mqueue /dev/pts /dev/shm /run /run/lxd_agent /sys /sys/fs/cgroup /sys/fs/pstore /sys/kernel/debug /sys/kernel/tracing

At this point we have been disconnected from VM and cannot reach it anymore.

> lxc shell centos-lxc
Error: LXD VM agent isn't currently running

Can this be fixed? Tnx!

P.S. tested with snapd 2.72-1.el9.

----

The Snapd team has forwarded me to LXD team:
https://bugs.launchpad.net/snapd/+bug/2136699/comments/1
Can you please help me have it fixed? Tnx!
```

### Expected behavior

The snapd should work on CentOS inside LXD to test Data artifacts (snaps).

### Actual behavior

CentOS is not reachable inside LXD VM once snapd is installed.

### Steps to reproduce

See above

### Information to attach

- [ ] Any relevant kernel output (`dmesg`)
- [ ] Instance configuration (`lxc config show <instance> --expanded`)
- [ ] Main daemon log (at `/var/log/lxd/lxd.log` or `/var/snap/lxd/common/lxd/logs/lxd.log`)
- [ ] If a lxc command fails, output of the command with `--debug`
- [ ] Output of the daemon with `--debug` (or use `lxc monitor` while reproducing the issue)
